YoY growth remains solid at +16.6% revenue and +21.8% EPS in the latest quarter, with strong iPhone demand (+22% YoY in Q3). However, the stock is expensive at  at 40x trailing P/E, near the top of its 30.5-43.1 range over the past year, elevated vs history. The Q3 earnings report (July 30) showed a services revenue miss ($30.74B vs $31.22B expected) and the stock fell ~9% after hours, with September quarter guidance of 9-11% growth below Q3's 16%. Regulatory headwinds on App Store economics and the CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus on Sept 1 add uncertainty. The Apple Upgrade leasing program with Klarna (launched July 28) and new Siri AI features could be modest catalysts, but the services miss and margin pressure outlook temper near-term upside. Balance sheet remains fortress-like with equity growing to $106.5B and debt declining to $82.7B.
